SwissArmyGrid 1.0.1: a hardening and speed release. Every part of the app was tested by trying to break it;
this release fixes what broke.

## Install or update

```bash
uv tool install --force "swissarmygrid[server]"   # the server
uv pip install -U swissarmygrid                   # the client, in your project's environment
```

Or the one-line installers from this release (`install.ps1` on Windows, `install.sh` on macOS and Linux).

## Fixed: things that did not work

- **Time-zone columns** (common from pandas) failed to show in every real install: the server install was
  missing `pytz`. The release check now pushes one, so this cannot ship broken again.
- **Copy transformations as code** never gave code that ran on your own table. Now "Copy as SQL" gives one
  DuckDB query over your table by its variable name, and "Copy as Python" gives `import duckdb` plus one
  line (`orders_view = duckdb.sql("""...""").df()`). The Copy buttons appear only after the server has run
  exactly the copied text on a copy of your table and matched the grid.
- **Scrolling** large tables jumped hundreds of rows per wheel notch (every table over 31,250 rows), and the
  row counter drifted from what was on screen.
- The **live connection** never came back after a drop, so later pushes opened new windows.
- Closing one side of a **compare** left the other grid showing the compare's rows.
- **Ctrl+C** copied nothing after clicking a header; a SQL result could land in the wrong tab.
- Pushing `Orders` after `orders` replaced the first table; a column named `rowid` emptied every grid;
  columns differing only in case were renamed without a word.
- Pandas pushes with duplicate or non-text column names, a MultiIndex, periods or complex numbers, and lists
  of records with missing keys, failed or arrived wrong.
- **Files**: Excel's Windows CSV encoding, one stray text value in a number column, JSON arrays of records,
  repeated headers and tab-separated `.txt` files now load. Excel dates before March 1900 export correctly.
- Profiles, charts and Key Finder no longer fail on NaN, infinity or columns named `k`, `n` or `m`.
- Two pastes in the same second no longer overwrite each other.

## Security and privacy

- Several ways around the **SQL box's read-only check** are closed (CTE scoping, self-references and table
  functions that could read other tables). Nothing could reach files or the network.
- An agent (through the MCP tools) could see values it should not at its privacy level: through DuckDB error
  messages, `string_agg` and other aggregates, JSON, PIVOT column names, renamed or derived columns that
  slipped past masks, and compare focus. Masks now follow each column back to its sources.
- An agent could **export without your click**, and could learn the server's token from returned links or by
  loading the connection file. Both are closed.
- The CSV header row is now protected against spreadsheet formula injection, like the cells.
- The connection file can no longer become readable by other users through a leftover temporary file.
- No cross-site scripting was found anywhere on the page (cells, headers, viewer, profile, charts, ERD, cards).

## Faster

| On 1,000,000 rows | 1.0.0 | 1.0.1 |
|---|---|---|
| Fetching rows while scrolling (each request) | ~48 ms | ~4 ms |
| Column profile (after a filter and sort) | 589 ms | 44 ms |
| Whole-table profile | 1.6 s | 0.11 s |
| SQL over the grid view (`... FROM grid LIMIT 100`) | 94 ms | 6 ms |
| CSV export | 6.2 s | 2.1 s |
| Sort, then the first rows | ~450 ms | ~210 ms |

The page also stopped leaking memory and event listeners for every closed grid, and makes 2 requests per
tab switch instead of 5.
